discovery: The theory of cosmic inflation and the quantum origin of cosmological structure
motivation: Guth proposed that an early epoch of exponential expansion solves the horizon, flatness and monopole problems. Linde made the idea viable with new and chaotic inflation, which are the basis of modern slow-roll models. Mukhanov, working with Chibisov, showed that quantum vacuum fluctuations stretched during inflation seed every galaxy, and he predicted a nearly scale-invariant, slightly red-tilted spectrum of adiabatic, Gaussian perturbations. COBE, WMAP and Planck have confirmed these predictions with striking precision, including a spectral index n_s ≈ 0.965, which differs from unity as predicted. Inflation turned the initial conditions of the universe from an assumption into a calculable consequence of quantum field theory in curved spacetime. It ties the most microscopic physics to the largest observed structures and has reshaped how physicists approach quantum gravity, de Sitter space and the early universe. It is one of the deepest and most fruitful theoretical ideas of the past half-century.
